item.title: Budget 2027: Manoel Island building to become a sailing facility
item.description: Sport Minister Byron Camilleri announced that an abandoned building on Manoel Island will be regenerated for use by the Malta Sailing Federation, which will make 60 watercraft available to sailing clubs under a Budget 2027 measure. The initiative forms part of wider regeneration plans for the island and of government plans to build a Malta Sport Hub, upgrade sporting facilities and give elderly people free access to SportMalta facilities.
item.content:encoded:

The initiative forms part of wider regeneration plans for the island and of government plans to build a Malta Sport Hub, upgrade sporting facilities and give elderly people free access to SportMalta facilities.

Sources: Malta Today

item.title: Man facing terrorism charges told court he sought out extremist preachers online
item.description: Police detailed Daniel Spiteri's internet searches at court on Tuesday, including videos of two Muslim preachers known to promote extremist views. Spiteri, 21, faces a series of terrorism-related charges including allegedly planning an attack, recruiting or inciting a person to commit terrorist activities and training or teaching an individual to use firearms for terrorism purposes. The court heard that seven more people have been arrested as part of the same investigation.

item.title: PN: Budget 2027 leaves the future of the animal hospital unresolved
item.description: The Nationalist Party said more than three years after the government shut the animal hospital, Budget 2027 left its future unresolved, asking what tangible results fishers, farmers, livestock breeders and animal owners would see from the Budget. The PN said students enrolled in veterinary-related courses have had to turn to small private clinics for practical training and would now have to find placements abroad.

item.title: Property deeds of sale fell while promise-of-sale deals rose in October, NSO reports
item.description: The National Statistics Office reported that in October 2026 the number of final deeds of sale relating to residential property amounted to 1,217, while promise of sale agreements rose to 1,408. The figures point to a shift from completed transactions to agreements still in progress in the Maltese property market.

Sources: Malta Independent

item.title: Motorcyclist grievously injured in St Paul's Bay crash
item.description: A 24-year-old motorcyclist suffered grievous injuries after a collision in Burmarrad Road, St Paul's Bay, at about 9.30am on Tuesday. Police said the crash involved a Toyota Ractis driven by a 55-year-old woman from St Paul's Bay and a Kymco Agility motorcycle ridden by the victim, a 24-year-old man from Bangladesh. The man was given medical assistance on site and taken to Mater Dei Hospital, where he was certified to have suffered grievous injuries. Police investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Man admits filming former colleagues in changing rooms
item.description: A 50-year-old man from Tarxien pleaded guilty on Tuesday to taking private intimate videos of former colleagues without their consent, and was granted bail pending sentencing. The court warned he could face up to five years' imprisonment, a fine of between €4,000 and €8,000, or both. Legal aid lawyer Martina Herrera asked the court to consider mitigating circumstances, noting the accused had a clean record and cooperated with police.

item.title: €3 million restoration project under way at San Anton Gardens
item.description: Conservation, maintenance and restoration works are ongoing at San Anton Gardens as part of a project costing more than €3 million, aimed at safeguarding one of Malta's most historically and architecturally important gardens. The works cover the conservation of the garden's historic features and are being carried out by the relevant heritage authorities.

item.title: CCTV footage used to retrace Marsa murder accused's movements, court hears
item.description: Police traced the movements of 34-year-old murder accused Isaac Asare through Marsa using CCTV footage after he was seen following 48-year-old Miriam Azzopardi into a field and later emerging alone. Azzopardi was found lifeless in the field on 23 September. Police Constable Andre Mifsud of the Major Crimes Unit testified that investigators gathered footage from several locations to identify the suspect. Asare is charged with murder and with stealing her mobile phone and other belongings, and pleads not guilty.

item.title: Żurrieq residents seek €10,000 to fight Nigret development plans
item.description: Residents of Żurrieq, together with the civil society group Il-Kollettiv, are crowdfunding to fund five planning appeals against the rezoning of a stretch of agricultural land in Nigret. The campaign had raised more than €2,000 by Tuesday afternoon, with the group saying this is its final chance to stop the development. The residents have previously crowdfunded successfully on the same issue and say the appeals will challenge the change in land use.

item.title: European Parliament backs Casa push for a stronger European Social Fund
item.description: The Employment and Social Affairs Committee backed proposals led by Maltese MEP David Casa and rapporteur Marit Maij to strengthen the European Social Fund in the next EU budget, which funds training, employment services and support for jobs, young people and families. Casa said the organisations delivering those services need certainty and that the fund should focus on workers, young people, families and children, noting the committee left the "My Voice, My Choice" initiative out of the text.

item.title: Magistrate calls for drug law reform after fatal ecstasy case
item.description: Nelson Esteban Lopez Ceron lost his bid to have his case heard by a drugs court after his wife, Sandra Zamudio, died in July 2022 after taking an ecstasy pill he allegedly gave her at Gianpula. Magistrate Caroline Farrugia Frendo said she believed the case was genuine but that "her hands were tied by the law", since a court-appointed psychologist found no drug dependency, a requirement for the drugs court. In her decree of 9 November she said such circumstances should be addressed by the legislator.

item.title: Malta is the only EU country objecting to the tobacco tax overhaul
item.description: Malta remains the sole member state resisting an EU bill that would overhaul tobacco taxation, introducing minimum rates on nicotine pouches, vapes and heated tobacco, and more than doubling the EU minimum cigarette tax. Finance Minister Clyde Caruana said taxation must remain a national prerogative, with Prime Minister Robert Abela personally intervening in talks with Ireland's prime minister. Estonia and Finland had also objected before withdrawing their reservations. Tax overhauls require unanimous approval from all 27 member states.

item.title: Artists' association and PEN Malta demand culture minister's resignation
item.description: The Malta Entertainment Industry and Arts Association opened a letter for artists and cultural workers to sign calling for Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea to resign, gathering more than 500 signatures by 8pm. The move follows remarks at the Festival of Ideas in which the minister described his first four months as "traumatic", called creativity "presumptuous and dangerous" and questioned why successful productions need public funding. PEN Malta separately demanded his resignation over the same speech.

item.title: Caruana says government ignored his population growth report for years
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana said the government has been warned since 2018 about problems stemming from rapid population growth, and that a nearly 300-page report he wrote detailing the pressure on housing, hospitals, schools and roads was ignored. Former Labour minister Evarist Bartolo said Caruana was warned about the report when he was still CEO of JobsPlus, and that it was shelved. Caruana expressed disappointment that people blame him for the government's policy, saying he was raising the consequences with his own cabinet.

item.title: Prison work becoming a 'luxury' for inmates, welfare commissioner warns
item.description: The prison welfare commissioner's 2025 annual report says work at Corradino Correctional Facility is so scarce it has become a "luxury", with too few placements and no transparent allocation system. The report also flags recurring summer heat problems and a revised operating procedure that remains unpublished. A 2024 National Audit Office report found only four inmates working outside the prison.

item.title: Enemalta spent €4.3 million upgrading Gozo's grid
item.description: Energy Minister Miriam Dalli told Parliament that Enemalta has invested €4,298,871 in substations and cables across Gozo since 2025, including about 15km of new 11kV medium-voltage lines in Xewkija, Qala, Għajnsielem, Marsalforn and Kerċem. Two new 33kV links and a further 132kV connection are under way, while feeders damaged in past storms have been replaced.

item.title: Nearly 7,900 chose to keep working instead of taking pension
item.description: Social Policy Minister Michael Falzon told Parliament that almost 7,900 people deferred their contributory pension between 2016 and 2024, while the number taking it at 61 fell from 1,254 to 864. Citing a Central Bank study, he said deferred pensions increase by 29 per cent by age 65, and that the government will not adopt measures that would undo a decade of progress in the field.

item.title: 2,500 glass bottles pulled from the Senglea seabed
item.description: Environmental NGO Żibel, with Investors Europe, mobilised 115 volunteers and divers at the Senglea waterfront who removed 1,543kg of waste, including more than 2,500 glass bottles weighing over a tonne. A diver described the accumulation as a "never ending mountain of glass bottles", underlining the scale of marine pollution around Malta's historic harbours.

item.title: Malta appointed co-facilitator for the 2027 UN development summit
item.description: Foreign and European Affairs Minister announced that through Ambassador Natasha Meli, Malta's Permanent Representative to the UN in New York, Malta has been appointed Co-Facilitator alongside Senegal to lead negotiations among UN member states ahead of the 2027 Sustainable Development Goals Summit. The role involves building consensus on a political declaration setting shared priorities for the run-up to 2030. The appointment was confirmed by the President of the 81st UN General Assembly session.

item.title: Mater Dei staff member accused of sexually harassing colleague granted bail
item.description: Sharoon Lazar, a 41-year-old Maltese citizen of Pakistani origin, pleaded not guilty to sexually harassing a woman who also works at Mater Dei Hospital and was granted bail. The alleged incident took place on 30 October at around 10.45pm. The prosecution opposed bail, citing concerns about interference with the alleged victim and about the accused leaving Malta as he also holds Pakistani citizenship and a Pakistani passport.

item.title: Man arrested at airport with 150 cannabis resin capsules in his stomach
item.description: Police arrested a 45-year-old Moroccan national at Malta International Airport after scans at Mater Dei Hospital showed about 150 capsules containing roughly 1.5kg of suspected cannabis resin with an estimated street value of €30,000. He had travelled from Morocco via Spain, arriving from Madrid, and was suspected of involvement in a drug-trafficking ring. Magistrate Philip Galea Farrugia opened an inquiry and appointed experts, with the suspect held pending court.

item.title: ADPD files FOI request for the government's eco-tax agreement with the MHRA
item.description: ADPD-The Green Party said on Tuesday it submitted a Freedom of Information request for a copy of the agreement between the Government and the Malta Hotels and Restaurants Association on the administration of the eco-tax, so the public can see how and where the money is collected and spent. The request was lodged with the Malta Tourism Authority, the Minister for Tourism and the Minister for Finance.

item.title: Sliema seafront bus lane to reopen in time for Black Friday
item.description: Enemalta said the first phase of cable works along the Gżira-Sliema front, part of a 4.5km 11kV cable plus 2.7km of low-voltage cables, will be completed by 26 November so the bus lane can reopen ahead of Black Friday and stay open through the Christmas shopping period. The lane is currently closed for excavation and cable-laying, with traffic out of Sliema reduced to one lane. Works were phased after talks with the Sliema Local Council and local businesses; the second phase starts on 4 January 2027.

item.title: Over 2,100 sign open letter calling for the culture minister's resignation
item.description: MEIA said more than 2,100 artists, cultural workers, organisations and members of the public signed its letter asking Prime Minister Robert Abela to request Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea's resignation. The letter follows the minister's Festival of Ideas remarks, in which he described his first four months in office as "traumatic" and said he oversees a portfolio where "everyone thinks they're God's gift to the world". Prime Minister Abela also said the comments about artists were insensitive.

item.title: Seismic signals recorded after Comino Crystal Lagoon cave collapse
item.description: The University of Malta Seismic Monitoring Research Group said recordings identified a seismic signal at around 9.13am on 8 November, detected by stations on Comino, Qala, Xlendi and Mellieħa, following the rockfall that blocked the entrance of the Crystal Lagoon cave on Sunday and pushed substantial debris into the lagoon. Preliminary estimates pointed to an origin west of Comino, consistent with the reported rockfall location. The cave is one of Comino's main natural attractions, visited by tourists and boat operators.

item.title: Edward Calleja appointed CEO of the energy and water regulator
item.description: The Regulator for Energy and Water Services announced Edward Calleja as its new Chief Executive Officer, leading executive operations with a focus on organisational effectiveness, sound governance and regulatory responsibility in Malta's energy and water sectors. Calleja was most recently Senior Partner at QP Limited, leading QP Consult and overseeing regional business development. REWS thanked Phyllis Micallef for her service as Acting Chief Executive.

item.title: 75-year-old man dies in Żurrieq after being crushed by his own truck
item.description: Pietru Grixti, 75, was certified dead at the scene after an Isuzu KC truck he was using reversed in an alley off Triq Wied Iż-Żurrieq at about 7.30am, trapping him between the vehicle and a rubble wall. Police were called at 7.30am to a reported fatal incident, and Civil Protection Department members and a medical team from Mater Dei Hospital attended. Magistrate Renata Farrugia is leading the inquiry, with police investigations still ongoing. Environment Minister Miriam Dalli, who lives near the family, paid tribute to the victim.

item.title: EU agriculture funds went to band clubs, sports facilities and fireworks factories
item.description: Agriculture Minister Anton Refalo told parliament, replying to PN MP Beppe Galea, that European funds from the Common Agricultural Policy were given to band clubs and sports organisations for projects unrelated to agriculture or heritage. The CAP Strategic Plan has a €166 million budget covering 2023 to 2027 and can be used to enrich rural heritage, while a notable chunk of the beneficiaries listed by the minister in the past two years are band clubs, religious organisations and sports facilities.

item.title: Criminal charges recommended as Salini fireworks blast inquiry concludes
item.description: The inquiry into the June 1 explosion at the Lourdes fireworks factory in Salini has concluded and is expected to recommend criminal charges against several individuals, Times of Malta understands. The findings have been submitted to the police and the Attorney General. The inquiry runs to over 4,000 pages and, according to sources, identifies several people deemed to have criminal responsibility, alongside others suspected of negligence or failing to act to prevent the blast, which razed the factory, damaged homes up to two kilometres away and burnt surrounding fields.
